activity.notes: Vonya was the prince of the Upper Narym Selkups and principal leader of the Piebald Horde, a Selkup-Ket military-political union. Russian records for 1596 describe roughly 400 warriors under his authority. He resisted Russian yasak demands and allied with Kuchum; the horde was decisively subordinated in 1598. ATLAS uses Piebald Horde rather than the broad modern ethnonym Selkup as the historical political community.

sources.title: Atlas of Indigenous Peoples of Russia — Selkup history
sources.citation_text: The official indigenous peoples atlas describes the Piebald Horde as a major Selkup military-political union led by Prince Vonya, with 400 warriors and resistance to Russian expansion.

sources.title: Ya. G. Solodkin — How the Peg Orda transformed into Narymsky volost
sources.citation_text: The scholarly article treats the Piebald Horde as a Middle Ob Selkup military-political union and identifies Vonya as its ruler during the Russian conquest.
